conventions: Complex frame carried by a proper preposition (rule 67): the frame rides undivided with the preposition and the governed noun stands bare, and this chapter heads the unit on the English word that realizes the preposition where the ASV writes one — 'for' in ἐπί → 'for the space of' at 19:8 and 19:10, 'touching' in περί → 'as touching' at 19:40 — and on the frame's lexical noun where the ASV writes none, ἐπί → 'the space of' headed on 'space' at 19:34. Rule 67 records the corpus as divided for a proper preposition; 19:34 is not a departure but the same arm with nothing prepositional in the frame to take the head.

An English preposition standing on an accusative complement: where the accusative is the verb's object, the preposition is the verb's own phrasal government and stays inside the verb's unit under rule 106 — 'speaking evil of' 19:9, 'that dwelt in' 19:10, 'I adjure … by' 19:13, 'dwelt at' 19:17, 'beckoned with' 19:33, 'blasphemers of' 19:37 — and the governed word keeps a bare noun or name. An adverbial accusative of duration is not that case: its 'for' realizes the duration and rides with the time noun, χρόνον → 'for a while' at 19:22, which is the same word the chapter gives to ἐπί where a preposition is expressed at 19:8 and 19:10. An oblique object is unaffected and keeps its case preposition: ἐπιθέντος αὐτοῖς → 'upon them' at 19:6, Ἐφέσου → 'at Ephesus' at 19:26, Σκευᾶ → 'of … Sceva' at 19:14.

Versification: the projection carries the Greek of ASV 19:41 — καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἀπέλυσεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν — at the end of 19:40. Under rule 37 those six source tokens are their own unrepresented units in 19:40 and all ten target tokens of 19:41 are `added`; neither verse reaches across, and no nearby English is stretched over the orphaned tokens. A reference comparison reports all six source tokens as disagreements and that report is not a correction.

A negator whose clause the ASV renders by a single positive English word joins the word it negates as one noncompositional unit, and an article standing between them is its own unrepresented unit under rule 93: οὐ τὰς τυχούσας → 'special' at 19:11, headed on the participle. Where the ASV instead writes an English negation word the pair splits in the ordinary way and the negator takes that word alone — οὐκ → 'no' with 'small' on ὀλίγος at 19:23, 'little' on ὀλίγην at 19:24, and 'gods' on θεοί at 19:26. The test is rule 45's, whether part of the English answers to a source token separately, and not whether the Greek is a litotes.
report: Checked all 79 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end for `added` units, which the lemma-keyed table cannot see. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one word differently, not one construction analysed two ways. ὁ divides cleanly by configuration: rules 19/21 where a determiner is written, rules 20/38/49 where a possessive or demonstrative already occupies the slot, rule 23 before a name or where the ASV writes no determiner, rule 32 where two English words stand for article+participle (19:4, 19:10, 19:13, 19:18, 19:22) against rule 90 where one stands (19:17, 19:26). τε/καί follow rule 70's count of English conjunctions at 19:6, 19:10, 19:12, 19:17, 19:27, 19:29. δέ, γάρ, οὖν, πρός, εἰς and λέγω vary only in the ASV's word.

Near-split (a), ἐπί + accusative of duration. The supplied frame rides undivided with the preposition at 19:8, 19:10 and 19:34; the heads differ only because the ASV writes 'for the space of' twice and 'the space of' once, and with no English preposition inside the frame at 19:34 the head has nowhere to sit but 'space'. περί → 'as touching' at 19:40 heads on 'touching', which is the same arm — the word realizing the preposition. One analysis, not two; recorded as a convention because rule 67 asks a chapter to say which arm it took.

Near-split (b), an English preposition standing on an accusative. Six units keep it inside the verb under rule 106 (19:9, 19:10, 19:13, 19:17, 19:33, 19:37); χρόνον → 'for a while' at 19:22 keeps it with the noun. Rule 106's arm is scoped in terms to an accusative *object*, and a duration accusative's 'for' is exactly the word the chapter gives ἐπί at 19:8 and 19:10, so the two readings are one analysis. Recorded as a convention, since the apparent contradiction is what a later reader would otherwise have to re-derive.

Near-split (c), the supplied juncture 'and'. Rule 88 puts it on the finite verb it introduces at 19:9, 19:15, 19:16, 19:25, 19:31 and 19:33. At 19:28 the expressed καί is left unrepresented because the ASV writes only that one 'and' and rule 65 gives an unwritten καί nothing; at 19:40 a supplied 'and' is `added` because what it introduces is a Greek relative clause the ASV de-subordinated, not a circumstantial participle, so rule 88 does not reach it and rule 86's test finds no token carrying coordination. Both verses flag the competing reading in their own notes; neither is a split from the rule 88 units.

Also checked and left standing: the litotes pair (οὐ τὰς τυχούσας → 'special' joined as noncompositional at 19:11 with the article empty under rule 93, against οὐκ → 'no' split from its adjective at 19:23, 19:24 and 19:26 — rule 45's test decides both); the two εἰ of 19:2, one empty as a direct-question marker and one aligned to the written 'whether'; ἐγένετο left empty at 19:34, where the ASV's recasting into 'all with one voice … cried out' leaves no English word for the existential verb while 'cried out' answers wholly to κραζόντων; and the rule 85 complementizers, placed on the non-finite complement at 19:1, 19:27 (three) and 19:35 without exception.

BSB: none of the 18 disagreements is a genuine error, and no accepted edge was touched to improve the rate. Six (19:40 τήν, καί, ταῦτα, εἰπών, ἀπέλυσεν, ἐκκλησίαν) are the rule 37 versification, which rule 37 says in terms will be reported and is not a correction; μέν at 19:32 is the report rule 70 predicts. The rest are documented convention differences: articles emptied by a displacing possessive or demonstrative (19:3, 19:12, 19:16, 19:25 ἡ), before a name (19:10), inside a noncompositional unit (19:11, rule 93), governing a substantival demonstrative (19:25 τά, rule 49); an unwritten intensifying καί (19:12, rule 65); a question-marking εἰ (19:2); and ἐγένετο at 19:34. BSB's 19:13 τόν '[by]' is the one live alternative, and it is not available to us either way — rule 21's determinerless clause would put a supplied 'by' on the name, never on the article.

No promotions. Two candidates were considered and declined for want of precedent rather than for want of merit, and are named here so a later chapter meeting them again can pick them up: the head of a complex frame that contains no English preposition (one unit, 19:34, and nearly forced by rule 17 anyway), and a negator joined to the word it negates where the ASV renders the negation by a single positive English word (one unit, 19:11). The precedent supplied for this chapter covers ὁ, καί, δέ, αὐτός, εἰμί, εἰς, λέγω, οὗτος and Παῦλος, and bears on neither.
